reason: The v16-02 block solved the balance problem and exposed the next binding constraint. Of 64 first episodes, 44 now survive the whole 6 s horizon on one foot (no falls, no right-skate replant) and every single one of them ends at com_speed 0.00 m/s: they glide, bleed all momentum and then stand balanced on the skate. Balance is no longer the limit; the momentum budget is. The measured glide decay is .256 m/s^2 and the measured glide-entry speed is median .546 m/s, so a 2.0 s credible glide needs .613 m/s at entry -- a shortfall of .080 m/s. The glide-entry peak was pinned at .546 m/s with a reward saturation of .38+.15=.53 m/s, i.e. the handoff term had exactly zero gradient over the whole interval where the policy needed to improve.
change: Widen the already-approved handoff term so the gradient survives above today's behaviour, without changing the frozen-expert reference: BRIDGE_HANDOFF_SPAN .15 -> .30 (full credit at .68 m/s, above the measured .613 m/s requirement) and BRIDGE_HANDOFF_GAIN 1.0 -> 1.2 (still below failure_cost 2.0, so a reckless lift that survives the .25 s hold and then falls still nets negative). The reference .38 m/s is unchanged, so every behaviour at or below the frozen public expert's ceiling still earns exactly zero and the v15/v16-02 optimum is untouched. The task-timing file microduck_onefoot_credit_bridge_env_cfg.py is also added to COMPATIBLE_SOURCES: the phase schedule (acceleration 2.0 s, lift 1.0 s, goal 2.0 s) is part of the task contract, but was previously not pinned by the continuation verifier at all.
